claims.text: Simultaneously increasing lightweight and oxide-forming elements favors formation of a single-phase solid solution in lightweight HEAs.
The resulting single-phase solid solution has significant lattice distortion.
The resulting multielement microstructure exhibits sluggish diffusion.
The proposed single-phase, lattice-distorted microstructure enhances mechanical strength.
The tuned composition promotes formation of a protective, adherent oxide film in corrosive environments and at elevated temperatures.
The synergy between the lattice-distorted solid solution and protective oxide film permits low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance to coexist.
A near-equiatomic baseline HEA lacking enhanced lightweight or oxide-forming fractions is typically high-density and only moderately performing.
Increasing the fractions of Al and Ti lowers the alloy's overall density.
The complex multielement environment increases lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases strength.
The complex multielement environment reduces diffusion rates.
Reduced diffusion rates improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Increasing Cr, Si, or Mo facilitates formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
A continuous protective oxide scale mitigates corrosion and high-temperature oxidative degradation.
Relative to the baseline, the tuned alloy will have lower density and similar or improved mechanical strength.
Relative to the baseline, the tuned alloy will show less mass loss and pit formation during salt-spray exposure.
Relative to the baseline, the tuned alloy will show improved oxidation resistance at 600–700°C through formation of a stable oxide scale.
Excessive lightweight-element content can cause phase instability, brittle intermetallic formation, or detrimental oxide phases that invalidate the proposed property combination.
Temperatures substantially above 700°C or highly aggressive corrosive media can exceed the protective capacity of the oxide scale.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits mechanical strength to remain similar to the baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvement in mechanical strength. A result with lower density, unchanged strength, and improved corrosion and oxidation resistance would therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger the stated falsification rule.
